QuestionStmt.S: Half life of a first order reaction is 3 minute. What is the time required to reduce the concentration of reactant by 90% of its initial concentration?

Solution.S:
For a first order reaction, $k = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{0.693}{3} = 0.231$ min⁻¹.

For 90% reduction, $[R] = 10\%$ of $[R]_0 = \frac{[R]_0}{10}$.

Using $k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \frac{[R]_0}{[R]} \right)$:

$$0.231 = \frac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \frac{[R]_0}{[R]_0/10} \right) = \frac{2.303}{t} \log(10)$$

$$0.231 = \frac{2.303}{t} \Rightarrow t = \frac{2.303}{0.231} = 9.97 \text{ min}$$

Thus the correct option is C: 9.97 minute.
